item.title: Russia Executes First-Ever Triple Arctic LNG Ship-to-Ship Transfer Amid Sanctions
item.description: Russia has for the first time conducted three simultaneous LNG ship-to-ship (STS) transfers in Arctic waters, a move highlighting Moscow’s increasingly sophisticated logistics network for exporting gas despite Western sanctions.

item.title: New Zealand Slaps Sanctions on 100 Russian ‘Shadow Fleet’ Vessels
item.description: New Zealand has imposed its largest-ever maritime sanctions package against Russia, designating 100 vessels linked to the country’s “shadow fleet” and lowering the price cap on Russian crude to $44.10 per barrel. The sweeping move significantly expands Wellington’s enforcement reach and aligns with broader international efforts to curb Moscow’s oil revenues.

item.title: India Grants One-Month Extension to Russian Marine Insurers
item.description: India temporarily extended permission for four Russian insurers to cover tankers calling at its ports, as the government seeks to sustain crude imports while also managing US pressure to end shipments from Moscow.

item.title: Canada, South Korea Partner to Rebuild Great Lakes Shipbuilding and Train Submarine Workforce
item.description: A major new partnership between South Korea’s Hanwha Ocean and Ontario Shipyards aims to bring large-scale shipbuilding back to Canada’s Great Lakes — while building the skilled workforce needed to support future submarine construction....

item.title: China Snaps Up Distressed Russian Oil Cargoes Shunned by India
item.description: Chinese refiners are snapping up Russian oil that India is shunning, helping Moscow to overcome a dip in purchases by the country that’s normally its biggest buyer of seaborne barrels.

item.title: Surging Oil Tanker Rates Tipped to Go Even Higher on Iran Risk
item.description: The cost to hire oil supertankers could be headed for the highest levels this decade on the growing risk of a major US attack on Iran, and as ownership of the vessels becomes more concentrated.

item.title: Trump Administration Advances Third ‘Big Beautiful’ Gulf Lease Sale as Offshore Program Gains Momentum
item.description: The Bureau of Ocean Energy Management announced Wednesday it will auction approximately 80.4 million acres of federal waters in the Gulf of America in August, marking the third offshore oil and gas lease sale under the Trump administration's accelerated energy development program.

item.title: Trump Slaps 10% Global Tariff Using New Trade Law After Supreme Court Defeat
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said on Friday that he would impose a 10% global tariff for 150 days to replace some of his emergency duties that were struck down by the U.S. Supreme Court.

item.title: Supreme Court Strikes Down Trump’s Global Tariffs in 6–3 Ruling
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court struck down on Friday President Donald Trump's sweeping tariffs that he pursued under a law meant for use in national emergencies, rejecting one of his most contentious assertions of his authority in a ruling with major implications for the global economy.

item.title: Supply Chains Brace for Renewed Turbulence as Supreme Court Strikes Down Trump Tariffs
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court delivered a landmark 6-3 ruling on Friday striking down President Donald Trump’s sweeping tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA), setting off a...
